tests.experiment: On the 78-problem K pool, restricted to problems where the RL-prefix continuation's opening text is at least as compressible as the own-prefix continuation's: how much more often does the RL-prefix arm finish than the own-prefix arm?
tests.recipe: Files s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_k-01/k_a/K_rl.jsonl, s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_k-01/k_a/K_own.jsonl and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/K_rl.jsonl (all rln4_gen rows). Define ratio(s) = len(zlib.compress(s.encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(s.encode('utf-8')) (Python zlib, level 9), and use the stored text field as it is. For each problem_index present in both modal_k-01 K_rl and K_own: take the row with the lowest sample in each file. Drop the problem if either text has len < 3000 characters. rR = ratio(modal K_rl text[:3000]); rO = ratio(K_own text[:3000]). Keep the problem only if rR <= rO. finish_rl = mean of (cap_hit == false) over the modal_k-01 K_rl row and, if one exists, the lowest-sample base_rl-02 K_rl row of the same problem_index (so 0, 0.5 or 1). finish_own = 1 if the K_own row has cap_hit == false, else 0. Statistic: mean over kept problems of (finish_rl - finish_own). Report the number of kept problems and how many of them have a base_rl-02 row.
tests.unit: difference in fraction of problems finished
tests.note: Files: s3 r4/modal_k-01/k_a/K_rl.jsonl (78 rows), r4/modal_k-01/k_a/K_own.jsonl (78 rows), r4/base_rl-02/out/K_rl.jsonl (69 rows), cached as runs/theory-tests/duel-r4-m01.turn2/{modal_K_rl,modal_K_own,base_rl-02_K_rl}.jsonl. The script downloads them with aws --profile iterate-ecr if they are missing. Every file holds only sample 0, so 'lowest sample' just picks that row. cap_hit is a bool in every row. Strictly cap_hit == false counts as finished; anything else (true, null) counts as not finished. Text is used exactly as stored, including the leading cue ' line!\n\nOkay'. The 3000-character drop rule applies to the two modal texts only: the base_rl-02 text is not length-checked, as the recipe says. ratio = zlib level-9 compressed bytes / UTF-8 bytes of text[:3000]. The keep test is rR <= rO, with exact float ties kept. Main number: mean over kept problems of finish_rl - finish_own, where finish_rl averages the modal K_rl row and the base_rl-02 row when one exists (0, 0.5 or 1). alt_measured (other reading): finish_rl from the modal K_rl row alone, as one 'RL-prefix arm' beside one own-prefix arm, without the AWS replicate. The counts the recipe asks for (problems kept, kept problems with a base_rl-02 row, problems in both files, problems dropped as short) are printed on the line before the JSON and on stderr. If no problem survives the filters, the script reports not_computable instead of a number.

tests.experiment: Among the cued base's rule-A loops at T 0.6 / top-p 1.0, does a more compressible opening bring the loop onset earlier (rank correlation of opening compressibility with onset position)?
tests.recipe: File iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl (run_cell rows). Keep rows with loop_A == true and onset_A_char present and >= 4000; drop all other rows. For each kept row compute s = len(zlib.compress(text[:3000].encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(text[:3000].encode('utf-8')) (Python zlib, level 9). Statistic: Spearman rank correlation between s and onset_A_char over the kept rows (scipy.stats.spearmanr, average ranks for ties). Report the number of kept rows.
tests.note: File: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl (500 run_cell rows; cell base_cue_math500_T0.6_p1, sampling T 0.6 / top-p 1.0), cached as runs/theory-tests/duel-r4-m01.turn2/abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa_answers.jsonl. The script runs modal volume get if the file is missing. The cached copy was copied from an earlier fetch in runs/theory-tests/ (same byte size as another session's copy); it was not re-downloaded. Filter: loop_A is True, and onset_A_char is a number >= 4000 (null or missing means dropped). s = zlib level-9 ratio of text[:3000], stored text with the leading cue. scipy is not an allowed import, so scipy.stats.spearmanr is reproduced in numpy: Pearson r of average ranks, ties given the mean rank. For 1-D inputs this equals spearmanr's correlation. One edge case: a row with text shorter than 3000 characters uses its whole text. An empty text would divide by zero, but a row whose loop onset is at 4000 or later cannot have empty text. alt_measured (other reading): the same rho over rows with onset_A_char >= 4000, ignoring the loop_A flag. It is likely identical to the main number, since an onset is normally recorded only for loops. The number of kept rows (and kept rows under the alt reading) is printed on the line before the JSON and on stderr. Fewer than 2 kept rows, or a constant variable, gives not_computable.
